increments.goal: A static coverage inventory (`scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`) that parses the whole fixture corpus, extracts every occurring rule-construct combination cell, diffs it against a machine-readable record of covered cells, and writes the uncovered cells to `docs/testing/worklist.json` — so the two skills of the later increments have a mechanical source of truth to work from.
criteria: `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` exists and parses every `.cat`/`.gst` file of both fixture sets (`src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`) statically, without rosters and without running the evaluator.

It records every occurring combination cell with occurrence count and file locations along these axes: constraint field-class x scope x flags (`shared`, `includeChildSelections`, `includeChildForces`, `percentValue`); condition type x scope x field-class; repeat attributes; modifier type x target-field-class; and the nesting constructs (`conditionGroup` types including `not`, `modifierGroups`, nested `repeats`).
The record of covered cells is machine-readable and the script diffs the inventory against it automatically; no human or agent has to read `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md` inside the loop.
The uncovered cells are written to `docs/testing/worklist.json`.
The script exits non-zero when the worklist is non-empty and zero when every occurring cell is covered.
The cell extraction is covered by unit tests, and they pass.

# Increment 1 — static coverage inventory, covered-cells diff, worklist

## What gets built

Three new source artefacts and one seeded data file:

1. `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.js` — the whole logic, pure and side-effect free at module level: classifiers, cell extraction from parsed XML documents, corpus walking, coverage derivation, diff, worklist building, exit-code rule.
2. `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` — a thin CLI: installs jsdom's `DOMParser`, calls the lib, writes `docs/testing/worklist.json`, prints a summary, sets the exit code. Mirrors the existing pair `scripts/lib/evaluator-measurement.js` + `scripts/measure-evaluator.js`.
3. `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` — the machine-readable manual record of covered cells (seeded, see below).
4. `docs/testing/worklist.json` — generated output, committed.

Plus two test files (see `testPlan`) and a two-line pointer at the top of `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md` saying the machine-readable record is now `covered-cells.json` + `worklist.json` and the matrix is human context only, never read inside the loop.

Write everything in English (comments, JSDoc, test names), even though neighbouring files are German — the shared brief overrides the local convention.

## Hard constraints that shape the design

- **No evaluator import.** `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` rule `evaluator-nur-ueber-fassade` has severity `error`: anything outside `src/evaluator/` may import only `src/evaluator/evaluator.js`. So the script must NOT import `src/evaluator/model.js` for `CountedFieldKind`/`ScopeKeyword`, however tempting. It defines its own vocabulary. This is also the right call in substance: the inventory is data-first and must stay independent of the engine (ADR 0033's black-box principle).
- **No roster, no evaluation.** Only `.cat`/`.gst` text is read; no `.ros`, no `evaluate()` call.
- **`scripts/**/*` is type-checked.** `tsconfig.json` includes `scripts/**/*` with `checkJs: true` (tests excluded via `**/*.test.js`). Both new source files need JSDoc types that satisfy `tsc --noEmit`.
- **`docs/testing/` is scanned by the E2E runner.** `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js:212` filters `readdirSync(..., {withFileTypes:true})` to `entry.isDirectory()`, so new *files* directly under `docs/testing/` are ignored by it. Safe.

## XML parsing

Use jsdom's `DOMParser`, exactly as `scripts/measure-evaluator.js` does (`globalThis.DOMParser = new JSDOM().window.DOMParser`). Measured on the real corpus: all nine files parse in **1.8 s total** (largest file 2.4 MB). A hand-rolled tag scanner was considered and rejected — it buys a second or two and risks false positives on tag-like text; jsdom is already a devDependency and already the project's Node-side XML seam.

The lib never touches `DOMParser` itself: its entry point takes already-parsed documents (`[{ file, doc }]`) or a `parseXml` callback. That is what makes the extraction unit-testable on small XML strings, and it lets the vitest jsdom environment supply the parser in tests without importing jsdom there.

After parsing, check each document for a `parsererror` element and fail loudly (exit 2) instead of silently reporting zero cells.

## Corpus

Two directories, `.cat`/`.gst` only (each also holds a `README.md`, which is skipped):
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` — 4 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`
- `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` — 3 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`

Nine files. Paths in the output are repo-relative and POSIX-separated, so the JSON is stable across machines. Derive the repo root from the module location (`fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`), like the other scripts do, so the run does not depend on the working directory.

## Symbol tables (first pass)

One pass over all documents collects, across the whole corpus (not per file — cost types live in the `.gst`, constraints in the `.cat`s):
- `costTypeIds` from every `<costType id=…>` (3 in this corpus),
- `characteristicTypeIds` from every `<characteristicType id=…>` (27),
- `constraintIds` from every `<constraint id=…>` (4365), together with the element, so a scenario's `limitId` can be looked up,
- an id→element index is only needed for constraints.

These tables are what turns a raw GUID in a `field` attribute into a class.

## Axis vocabularies

**Scope class** (`constraint`/`condition`/`repeat`): the literal keyword if it is one of `roster`, `force`, `parent`, `self`, `unit`, `ancestor`, `primary-catalogue`, `category`; a GUID (anything else non-empty) collapses to `id`; a missing attribute is `absent`. Source: `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §13.1 and the `scope="unit"`/`scope="ancestor"` box in §7.7. Collapsing GUIDs is essential — the corpus holds 8 distinct id-scopes and keeping them apart would make the worklist a list of catalogue rows instead of a list of constructs. In this corpus `category` never occurs as a literal.

**Counted field class** (`constraint`/`condition`/`repeat` `field`, per §13.2): `selections`→`selectionCount`, `forces`→`forceCount`, `limit::<id>`→`limitValue`, an id in `costTypeIds`→`costSum`, anything else→`unresolvedField`, missing→`absent`.

**Modifier target field class** (`modifier` `field`, per §7.7/§13.2): the literals `hidden`, `name`, `category`, `error`, `warning`, `info`, `sortIndex`, `page` stay themselves; an id in `costTypeIds`→`costValue`; in `characteristicTypeIds`→`characteristic`; in `constraintIds`→`constraintValue`; `limit::<id>`→`limitValue`; anything else→`unresolvedTarget`; missing→`absent`. **Finding:** three modifier `field` ids in the corpus (`ce6e-afde-2ed1-aac2`, `a59d-2ddb-429c-1aca`, `410e-ed97-ecf8-cfa4`, 7 occurrences) exist nowhere in the corpus as an `id` attribute — dangling references. They must land in one `unresolvedTarget` bucket, not one cell each, and the raw ids belong in that cell's examples.

**childId class** (`condition`/`repeat`, per §13.2): `model`, `unit`, `upgrade`, `any` stay literal; anything else non-empty→`id`; missing→`absent`.

**Flag normalization — the single most important decision.** An omitted `shared`/`includeChildSelections`/`includeChildForces`/`percentValue`/`roundUp` is normalized to the XSD default before it enters the key: `shared=true`, `includeChildSelections=false`, `includeChildForces=false`, `percentValue=false` (`src/parser/schema/Catalogue.xsd:428-431`), `roundUp=false` (`Catalogue.xsd:545`). Without it the corpus splits into cells that differ only in serialization noise — measured: 32 raw constraint cells collapse to **22** normalized ones, and the two largest "different" cells (2523 and 542 occurrences) are the same cell. Put the defaults in one frozen constant with the XSD line numbers in the comment. `repeats` is `use="required"` in the XSD and is bucketed `1` vs `gt1` instead of being normalized.

## The cell key

A `|`-joined string, stable and greppable, with the same axes also present structurally on the record. Seven kinds:

- `constraint|<type>|<fieldClass>|<scopeClass>|s=<shared>|ics=<includeChildSelections>|icf=<includeChildForces>|pct=<percentValue>`
- `condition|<type>|<scopeClass>|<fieldClass>|child=<childIdClass>`
- `repeat|<fieldClass>|<scopeClass>|child=<childIdClass>|repeats=<1|gt1>|roundUp=<flag>|pct=<flag>`
- `modifier|<type>|<targetFieldClass>`
- `conditionGroup|<type>|<top|nested>` — `nested` when the group's grandparent element is itself a `conditionGroup` (`conditionGroup > conditionGroups > conditionGroup`)
- `modifierGroup|cond=<bool>|repeats=<bool>|<top|nested>` — `cond` is true when the group carries a `<conditions>` or `<conditionGroups>` child, `repeats` when it carries a `<repeats>` child, `nested` by the same grandparent rule
- `repeatList|n=<1|gt1>|on=<modifier|modifierGroup>` — one per `<repeats>` list element; this is the axis that distinguishes "several `<repeat>` in one list" from a single one

Two deliberate departures from the criteria's literal wording, both recorded here as decisions:
- **Constraint `type` (`min`/`max`) is part of the constraint key** although the criterion names only field-class × scope × flags. `min` and `max` are different code paths and the matrix's first two rows are exactly this; leaving it out would merge them. Costs nothing (22 cells).
- **`childId` class is part of the condition key** although the criterion names only type × scope × field-class. §7.7 documents two encodings of a `forceEntry` instance check (`scope=<forceId> childId=any` vs `scope=force childId=<forceId>`), and type-keyword counting (`model`/`unit`/`upgrade`) is a distinct path from id counting (Issue 078). Costs about 11 extra cells (39 instead of ~28). Every criterion still holds — the cells are recorded along the named axes, only refined.

Rejected alternatives: keeping raw scope/field GUIDs as their own cells (turns 101 cells into hundreds of catalogue rows); one cell per dangling modifier target id (same problem); a `conditionGroup` axis for member fan-out (the matrix already records that fan-out is not a separate code path).

**Measured result of this design on today's corpus: 101 distinct cells** — constraint 22, condition 39, repeat 7, modifier 22, conditionGroup 5, modifierGroup 4, repeatList 2, over 9375 construct occurrences. That is a worklist a campaign can actually work down; it is the number the implementation should reproduce.

## Cell record

Per cell: `key`, `kind`, `axes` (the structured components), `occurrences` (total), `files` (`[{ file, occurrences }]`, sorted by path) and `examples` — at most **3**, in corpus/document order, each `{ file, elementId, anchorTag, anchorId, anchorName, path }` where the anchor is the nearest ancestor element carrying both `id` and `name` (the `selectionEntry`/`categoryEntry`/`forceEntry`/`entryLink` the construct hangs on) and `path` is the tag chain from the document root joined by `>`.

jsdom gives no line numbers, so "file locations" are file path + anchor id/name instead. That is deliberately more useful to the black-box scenario author of increment 2, who searches the catalogue by id, than a line number would be.

## Where "covered" comes from

Two sources, unioned:

1. **Derived automatically from the existing scenario manifests, on every run.** Every `docs/testing/*/scenario.json` declares `rosters[].expect.firing[].limitId` and `rosters[].expect.absent[]` (a plain id string). Those ids are constraint ids. Look each one up in the constraint index and mark that constraint's cell covered, with the scenario directory name as evidence. Measured: 38 manifests pin 73 distinct ids, 70 of which resolve to a constraint, and they cover **15 of the 22** constraint cells. This is what puts the existing coverage into the loop mechanically, without anyone reading `constraint-matrix.md` — and it can never go stale, because it is recomputed rather than transcribed. An id that resolves to nothing is reported as an unmatched-evidence line, never a crash.
2. **`docs/testing/covered-cells.json`, the manual record** — for cells no manifest id can attest (condition, modifier, repeat, group families) and for waived cells. Shape: `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "cells": [ { "key": "…", "evidence": ["docs/testing/<scenario>" | "unit test <path> <name>"], "rationale": "…" } ] }`. This is the file increment 2's skill appends to when it lands a green scenario.

**Seed the manual record with exactly one entry** and nothing more: `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|parent|selectionCount|child=id`, one occurrence (Orcs and Goblins, "ergofang"), rationale: not an XSD condition type (`docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §13.1), reported as `unsupportedCondition` and evaluated fail-closed — there is no catalogue-derivable semantics to pin. Do **not** transcribe the rest of `constraint-matrix.md` into the record: its rows are per-attribute prose, not per-cell, and a guessed seed would silently hide genuinely uncovered cells. Fail-closed is the project's own principle here — an over-large worklist costs the campaign work, a wrong seed costs it a blind spot.

Expected first worklist: about **85** cells (101 minus 15 derived minus 1 waived).

## Diff, output, exit code

`docs/testing/worklist.json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedBy": "scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js",
  "corpus": ["src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive", "src/__fixtures__/whfb6"],
  "totals": { "cells": 101, "covered": 16, "uncovered": 85 },
  "cells": [ …the uncovered cell records… ]
}
```

Sorted by `occurrences` descending, then `key` ascending — deterministic. **No timestamp and no run id**: a generated file that changes on every run would dirty the working tree forever and make the drift guard impossible.

Stdout: one summary block — cells by kind, covered by derivation, covered by record, uncovered, plus any stale or unmatched evidence — then the top uncovered cells. Warnings never change the exit code.

Exit codes: **0** when the worklist is empty, **1** when it is not, **2** on an operational failure (a corpus directory missing, a `parsererror`, unreadable JSON). Two guards report but do not fail: a key in `covered-cells.json` that no longer occurs in the corpus (stale), and a key whose syntax does not parse. Deadlocking the loop on bookkeeping is worse than a warning line.

**Running the script today exits 1, and that is the correct outcome** — the worklist is non-empty by construction until the campaign of increments 2 and 3 has run. It is therefore deliberately not one of the `checks`; the drift-guard test covers the same ground without a red gate.

## Order of work

1. lib: classifiers + `cellKey` + extraction over injected documents.
2. lib: corpus walk, manifest-derived coverage, manual record read, diff, worklist build, exit-code rule.
3. CLI wrapper.
4. Seed `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`; run the CLI once to generate `docs/testing/worklist.json`; commit both.
5. Pointer line in `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md`.

## Whether

Tests are needed. The extraction is pure logic over XML and the criteria demand unit tests for it.

## Conventions and their documentation

**There is no test-suite doc and no `CLAUDE.md` in any test directory.** The only `CLAUDE.md` in the repository is the root one (a symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`); `docs/testing/` holds scenario directories and `constraint-matrix.md`, no agent doc. The nearest thing to a suite doc is ADR 0006 (`docs/adr/0006-testing-and-automation.md`), which fixes vitest as the unit framework, the zero-tolerance rule, and the `docs/testing/` manifest runner — but says nothing about how a `scripts/` test is written. Write the missing directory doc as part of the test step if the role calls for it; nothing existing contradicts what follows.

Observed conventions to follow, from `scripts/lib/evaluator-measurement.test.js`, `scripts/generate-schema-module.test.js` and `scripts/rules-crawler.test.js`: named imports from `vitest` (`describe, it, expect`), the module under test imported relatively, no global setup beyond `vitest.config.js` (environment `jsdom`, globals on, `src/test-utils/i18nTestSetup.js`). Because the environment is jsdom, **`DOMParser` is already a global in tests** — the test files need no jsdom import of their own; build documents with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, 'application/xml')`. Existing script tests carry German comments; write yours in English, per the shared brief.

Nothing is faked or mocked: the lib is pure and the corpus is a frozen fixture.

## What — file 1: `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.test.js`

Unit tests over tiny synthetic XML strings (a `<catalogue>` root with a handful of constructs, plus `<costType>`/`<characteristicType>` declarations where a class depends on them). Level: unit. Framework: vitest. Command: `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.test.js`.

Criterion "records every occurring combination cell … along these axes":

1. A constraint `type=max field=selections scope=parent shared=true includeChildSelections=false includeChildForces=false percentValue=false` yields exactly the key `constraint|max|selectionCount|parent|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|pct=false`, with `occurrences` 1 and the given file path recorded.
2. Flag normalization: the same constraint with `includeChildForces` and `percentValue` omitted yields the **same** key, and the two occurrences merge into one cell with `occurrences` 2 and both files listed.
3. Explicit non-default flags are not collapsed: `shared="false"` yields a key distinct from `shared="true"`.
4. `type="min"` and `type="max"` on otherwise identical constraints yield two cells.
5. Counted field classes: `selections`→`selectionCount`; `forces`→`forceCount`; an id declared as `<costType>`→`costSum`; `limit::<that id>`→`limitValue`; an id declared nowhere→`unresolvedField`; the attribute missing→`absent`.

## What this increment is

A complete coverage inventory already exists on this branch (inherited from the blocked inc-1: `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`, `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.js`, `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.js`, their two test files, `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`, `docs/testing/worklist.json`, `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md`). Do not rewrite it. This increment closes the two findings that blocked it and re-delivers the whole as accepted. Everything else in the criteria list is already satisfied by the inherited code; the facts proving that are below, so nobody has to re-derive them.

## Fact base (measured during this research, on this branch)

- The corpus is 9 files: 5 in `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` (4 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`), 4 in `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` (3 `.cat` + 1 `.gst`). Each `README.md` is skipped by the extension filter. No parse failures.
- The inventory yields 105 cells. Corpus occurrence totals: constraint 5290, condition 1739, conditionGroup 261, modifier 1762, modifierGroup 121, repeat 214, repeats (`repeatList`) 213.
- 924 constraint ids occur in both fixture sets. Exactly 2 of them classify into different cells: `1077-7379-f142-f382` (`min|selectionCount`, scope `force` in the definitive `.gst`, scope `roster` in the whfb6 `.gst`) and `d818-c60d-b1f8-8aaa` (same, `max`). One further id (`dfc9-fce8-cc2a-b997`) occurs in three files but classifies identically everywhere.
- 38 scenario manifests. Manifest shape: top-level `dataset: { gameSystem?, catalogues[] }`, and each entry of `rosters[]` may carry its own `dataset` that **overrides** (not merges) the manifest one. 7 manifests use roster-level overrides (`violation-classification` has four). The runner's rule is `rosterCase.dataset ?? manifest.dataset` (`src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js:258`); mirror it exactly.
- Dataset paths are repo-relative, POSIX-separated strings, byte-identical to what `repoRelative()` produces for the corpus files — so a plain string match against the index resolves them, with no path normalization needed.
- Two manifests (`group-scope-missing-mandatory`, `parent-scope-missing-mandatory`) declare a third fixture set, `scripts/__fixtures__/showcase-empire/`, which is outside the inventoried corpus. One manifest (`vampire-bloodlines-ergofang`) declares the `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` set. All the rest declare the definitive set.
- `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §13.3 calls `id` a unique identifier — unique *within a dataset*. The two fixture sets are two editions of the same data, which is why one id can carry different attributes across them. Per-file resolution is therefore well defined, and the real corpus confirms it: zero ambiguous resolutions.

## Finding 1 — wrong-cell evidence crediting

`extractCells` builds `index` as a flat `Map<constraintId, cellKey>` (`evaluator-coverage-cells.js:509,516`). The corpus walk visits the definitive set first and the whfb6 set second, so for a duplicated id the whfb6 entry wins. `coveredKeysFromManifests` then looks the id up in that flat map, regardless of which files the scenario runs against.

Measured consequence today: the three definitive-set scenarios `docs/testing/ogre-kingdoms`, `docs/testing/orcs-and-goblins` and `docs/testing/vampire-counts` reference `1077-7379-f142-f382`, and their evidence is credited to `constraint|min|selectionCount|roster|s=true|ics=true|icf=true|pct=false` (the whfb6 `.gst` cell) instead of `constraint|min|selectionCount|force|s=true|ics=true|icf=true|pct=false` (the definitive `.gst` cell they actually exercise). `d818-c60d-b1f8-8aaa` is referenced by no manifest, so it is unaffected.

### Fix 1a — a per-file constraint index

In `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.js`, change `extractCells`'s `index` from `Map<string, string>` to `Map<string, Map<string, string>>`: outer key the repo-relative file, inner map constraint id to cell key. Build it in the existing walk, where `tag === Tag.CONSTRAINT && elementId !== null` already fires:

```js
let fileIndex = index.get(file);
if (fileIndex === undefined) { fileIndex = new Map(); index.set(file, fileIndex); }
fileIndex.set(elementId, built.key);
```

Update the `Inventory` typedef and the `@returns` doc. Document that a repeated id inside one file is last-wins, since a dataset guarantees id uniqueness and the corpus holds no such case.

### Fix 1b — per-roster dataset resolution

Rewrite `coveredKeysFromManifests(manifests, index)` (same name, same arity, same `{ matched, unmatched }` return) to resolve each roster separately:

1. Per roster, take `roster.dataset ?? manifest.dataset ?? null`, and flatten it to a file list `[dataset.gameSystem, ...(dataset.catalogues ?? [])]` keeping only non-empty strings.
2. Collect the roster's ids exactly as today: every `expect.firing[].limitId` and every `expect.absent[]` entry (string form, or object form via `limitId ?? id`).
3. Resolve each id only against those files: `index.get(file)?.get(id)`. Every distinct key found becomes a `matched` entry `{ key, id, evidence: manifest.dir }`, deduplicated on `` `${key} ${evidence}` `` as today.
4. An id resolving to no key becomes an `unmatched` entry, which now also carries a `reason`:
   - `'unknown-id'` — the id names no constraint anywhere in the corpus. Derive the corpus-wide id set inside the function as the union of the inner maps' keys, so no new parameter is needed.
   - `'outside-dataset'` — the id names a corpus constraint, but none of the roster's declared files hold it. This is the alarm that a scenario's dataset declaration and its expectations have drifted apart; the real corpus produces zero of these today.

Measured outcome of the fix over the real corpus and manifests: 15 manifest-derived covered keys before and after; exactly one swaps. Union with `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` (one waived cell) stays 16 covered, 89 uncovered, 105 cells. No ambiguous id. Unmatched stays at the same three distinct ids as today — `02cd-cabf-7e25-2b09` and `d96c-c95f-8224-7c87` (showcase-empire, outside the corpus) and `budget::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249` (a synthetic roster-budget id, not a constraint) — all three `unknown-id`.

### Fix 1c — CLI warnings

In `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`, split the existing unmatched warning line by `reason`, so the two failure modes read apart, e.g. `WARNING manifest id names no constraint in the corpus: <id> (<dir>)` and `WARNING manifest id names a corpus constraint outside the scenario's dataset: <id> (<dir>)`. ### 1. What this skill does (3-5 sentences)

It closes evaluator coverage cell by cell, data-first: the catalog corpus says which rule constructs exist, the inventory says which of them no scenario pins yet, and the loop pins the next one with a black-box E2E scenario. State the inversion explicitly: the search starts from the data, never from a hypothesis about the engine code. Name ADR 0033 as the reason.

### 2. Preconditions (short list)

- Read `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` before the first cell — it is the canonical vocabulary of every axis in a cell key and takes precedence over the ADRs.
- Work on a feature branch; if the current branch is the repository default branch, create one first. Never create a git worktree (the old skill's first step; it is dropped because the campaign driver owns the branch).
- One invocation completes exactly one cell. The caller re-invokes for the next one; the per-run cap belongs to the campaign driver, not here.

### 3. Step 1 — run the inventory

- Command: `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` from the repository root.
- Exit codes, verbatim from the script's header: `0` every occurring cell is covered or waived — there is nothing to do, report that and stop; `1` the worklist is not empty — **this is the loop's normal state, not a failure**, continue; `2` an operational failure (missing corpus directory, `parsererror`, unreadable JSON) — stop and report, do not work around it. Say plainly that a tool wrapper flagging exit 1 as an error must not be read as a failure.
- `WARNING` lines do not change the exit code. Act on one only when it names a scenario this loop just wrote: `WARNING manifest id names no constraint in the corpus` means the manifest's `limitId` is wrong, and `WARNING manifest id names a corpus constraint outside the scenario's dataset` means its `dataset` and its expectation disagree — send the scenario back to the author before committing. A `WARNING stale covered key` names a `covered-cells.json` entry the corpus no longer holds; report it, do not silently delete it.

### 4. Step 2 — take the next cell

- Read `docs/testing/worklist.json`. `cells` is sorted heaviest first (`sortCells`: occurrences descending, then key ascending), so the next cell is the first entry that is not already parked in `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` and has no scenario in progress.

- Prefer an example under `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/`. Where every occurrence of the cell sits under `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`, the scenario author cannot read it — its allow-list (`docs/agents/e2e-testcase-author.md`) covers the definitive corpus only — so park the cell with the question whether the allow-list should be extended to the upstream corpus, and take the next cell. Four of today's 89 uncovered cells are in that position.

### 5. Step 3 — derive the rule the cell demands, from data only

- Sources, and only these: the catalog XML the example names, `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md`, `src/parser/schema/Catalogue.xsd`, and the BSData wiki submodule under `docs/bsdata-catalogue-development-wiki/`.
- Never open `src/evaluator/*.js` in this mode. A rule read off the engine cements the engine's bugs as expectations.
- The output of this step is one plain-language sentence — what the catalog data demands of a correct evaluator for this construct — plus the evidence: the file, the ancestor entry id and name, and the element's attributes.
- Where that sentence cannot be justified from those sources, park the cell (step 7) and continue with the next one.

### 6. Step 4 — delegate the scenario to `e2e-testcase-author`

- Delegate; never write the scenario in the main conversation. The subagent's premise (`docs/agents/e2e-testcase-author.md`) takes `rule` (required, plain language), `scenario_name` (required, the slug of the new directory under `docs/testing/`), and an optional dataset hint.
- The slug is kebab-case and describes the construct, in the style of the existing directories (`modifier-group-repeats`, `condition-group-not`); check that `docs/testing/<slug>/` does not exist yet.
- The delegation prompt carries: the rule sentence, the slug, the dataset hint (the `gameSystem` and `catalogues` paths the example's file implies), the catalog evidence from `examples[]`, and which manifest key must carry the expectation (table below). It carries **no** engine code, no engine output, and no statement about what the engine currently does — quoting any of that into the prompt destroys the black-box premise the whole campaign rests on.
- Which manifest key pins which kind of cell (from the manifest contract in `docs/agents/e2e-testcase-author.md`):
  - `constraint` → `expect.firing` / `expect.absent` with the constraint's `limitId`, `actual` and `bound`. Only this kind is credited automatically, because `coveredKeysFromManifests` resolves manifest `limitId`s against the roster's dataset.
  - `condition` / `conditionGroup` → two rosters that make the gated constraint or modifier fire and not fire, so the condition's own semantics is what the pair distinguishes.
  - `modifier` / `modifierGroup` → `expect.capabilities` (`name`, `isHidden`, `effectiveMin`/`effectiveMax`, `characteristics`, `infoElements`) or, for a `field="error"|"warning"|"info"` modifier, `expect.messages` with `origin: "authorMessage"`.
  - `repeat` / `repeatList` → `expect.capabilities` on the slot whose bound or value the repetition moves, with a roster whose count crosses at least two repetitions.
- The author reports back a summary, including any gap that made it stop. A gap it reports is a park (step 7), not a reason to write the scenario yourself.

### 7. Step 5 — run the evaluator tests

- Command, exactly: `npx vitest run src/evaluator`. This is the criterion's command; the change touches only `docs/testing/`, which that suite consumes, so no other suite is run here.
- Isolate the new scenario's cases with `npx vitest run src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js -t "Szenario: <slug>"` — the runner names its dynamic cases `Szenario: <manifest.name>` and, per roster, `<label>: Bericht entspricht der deklarierten Erwartung`.
- Only failures naming the new scenario decide green or red. Other evaluator failures are the campaign's already-pinned gaps and are neither this cell's result nor this skill's to fix. Note here that `CLAUDE.md`'s "all unit tests must pass" is suspended for the pinned red scenarios recorded in `campaign-state.json`, each of which phase B closes.

### 8. Step 6 — green: keep the scenario and mark the cell covered

- Never change a scenario's expectations to make the engine pass, and never soften, delete or narrow an assertion for that purpose. State this as its own forbidding sentence — it is the rule that separates this loop from a rubber stamp. A wrong expectation is corrected only when the *catalog data* proves it wrong, and then by the author subagent, with the corrected derivation written into the scenario README.
- Mark the cell covered: re-run `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` first. If the cell has left the worklist, the manifest derivation already credits it (that happens for `constraint` cells pinned by a `limitId`) and no manual entry is added — the file's own `_comment` reserves manual entries for cells no manifest `limitId` can attest. Otherwise append to `docs/testing/covered-cells.json`: `{ "key": "<cell key>", "evidence": ["docs/testing/<slug>"], "rationale": "<which roster and which assertion pin it>" }`, then run the inventory again so `docs/testing/worklist.json` is regenerated from the new record. Only `key` is read by the tooling; `evidence` and `rationale` are for the human reader.
- Update `docs/testkatalog-evaluator-e2e.md` in the same step: the catalog and the scenario stock are kept identical by hand, in German, with no generator and no CI gate.
- Commit everything of the cell together — the scenario directory, `covered-cells.json`, the regenerated `worklist.json` and the Testkatalog entry — in one commit, e.g. `test(coverage): pin <cell key> with scenario <slug>`.
- Verify the bookkeeping with `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js`; its drift guard recomputes the worklist from the corpus and deep-equals the committed file, so a forgotten regeneration is caught there.
- A committed green scenario is never deleted. Campaign progress is monotone.

### 9. Step 7 — red: pin the gap

- A red scenario stays exactly as it is. Deleting it, or weakening it, throws away the only evidence of the gap.
- Mark the cell covered by the same rule as a green one: covered means *pinned by a scenario*, not *passing*. A red cell that stayed in the worklist would be handed out again on the next invocation and the loop would never finish phase A, while a red `constraint` cell leaves the worklist automatically through the manifest derivation — the two kinds must not diverge. The `rationale` says the scenario is red and points at the `pinnedGaps` entry.
- Append the phase-B task to `campaign-state.json` `pinnedGaps` with the shape above, and commit it with the scenario, the coverage record, the regenerated worklist and the Testkatalog entry.
- Report the gap in the run summary: the cell, the scenario, the failing case labels, and what the catalog data demands.

### 10. Step 8 — park an underivable cell

- Park when the intended semantics cannot be derived from the catalog data, the BSData wiki or the XSD; when the author subagent reports a gap it could not close; or when the cell occurs only in the corpus outside the author's allow-list.
- Append to `campaign-state.json` `parkedQuestions`, commit it, and continue with the next cell in the same invocation. A parked cell is skipped in step 2 while its `status` is `open`.
- The question is phrased so a human can answer it without opening a file. The human's answer is written into the entry's `answer` with `status: "answered"`; a cell whose question is answered is picked up again like any other worklist entry, and the answer is quoted into the delegation prompt as part of the rule.
- A cell that is genuinely untestable — the construct is outside the format specification and there is no catalog-derivable semantics at all — is waived instead, as a `covered-cells.json` entry with `"evidence": ["waived"]` and a rationale, exactly like the existing `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|…` entry. Park is temporary and waive is permanent; do not waive to get rid of a question.

### 11. Secondary mode — the engine-code hypothesis search

- Keep it, explicitly scoped: it is for suspected *semantics bugs inside cells the worklist already counts as covered*, not for finding uncovered cells. The worklist is the only source of new cells.
- The flow: analyse `src/evaluator/` thoroughly, form a hypothesis grounded in that analysis about a case the engine gets wrong, confirm the construct really occurs in the corpus, and delegate the scenario.
- Two rules carry over from the primary mode and must be repeated here in one sentence each: the delegation prompt still carries only a data-derived rule and never engine code or engine output, and the resulting scenario is kept whether it is green or red — a green one because progress is monotone, a red one as a pinned gap under step 9. This is the one deliberate departure from the old skill, which deleted a green test; say so, so nobody restores the old behaviour.

### 12. Never (closing list, one line each)

- Never change a scenario's expectations to make the engine pass.
- Never delete or weaken a committed scenario.
- Never write scenario files in the main conversation instead of delegating.
- Never read `src/evaluator/*.js` in the primary mode, and never quote engine code or engine output into a delegation prompt in either mode.
- Never change production code under `src/evaluator/` — that is phase B's work.
- Never propose a version bump for this work: scenarios and tooling are not user-facing.

## Decisions, including the rejected ones

- **Covered means pinned, not passing.** Chosen because `coveredKeysFromManifests` already credits a `constraint` cell the moment a manifest names its `limitId`, green or red; leaving red cells of the other kinds in the worklist would both contradict that and make phase A non-terminating. The issue's termination criterion (worklist empty **and** every scenario green **and** no parked question open) only makes sense under this reading — otherwise the second clause would be redundant. Rejected: a third `pinnedRed` bookkeeping state in `covered-cells.json`; the tooling reads only `key`, so a new state would need a code change this increment must not make, and `campaign-state.json` already carries the red list.
- **`campaign-state.json` under `docs/testing/`, one file with two arrays.** Chosen so "the campaign state" is a concrete path both this skill and the inc-3 driver name, next to the two coverage files. Rejected: two files (`pinned-gaps.json`, `parked-questions.json`) — more paths for the same lifecycle; and recording gaps directly into a campaign issue markdown file — that couples the explorer to an issue-file format inc-3 owns.
- **The manual covered entry is conditional on the cell surviving a regeneration.** Chosen because `covered-cells.json`'s own `_comment` reserves it for cells no manifest `limitId` can attest; an unconditional entry would duplicate the derivation and go stale as a `WARNING stale covered key` the moment the corpus moves. The criterion "marked covered in `covered-cells.json`" is satisfied in every case where the record is the thing that credits the cell.
- **Upstream-only cells are parked, not attempted.** The author's read allow-list covers `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` only, while `docs/testing/vampire-bloodlines-ergofang/` shows scenarios against `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` do exist. Extending the allow-list is a change to `docs/agents/e2e-testcase-author.md` and ADR 0033's contract — a human decision, which is exactly what a parked question is for. Rejected: quoting the upstream XML into the delegation prompt so the author never opens the file; that makes the explorer the author's eyes and moves derivation into an agent that is not the black-box one.
- **English, replacing a German skill file.** The shared brief requires English for everything landed in the repository. The `description` keeps a German clause so a German-language user request still matches the skill.
- **No worktree step.** The old step 1 created a dedicated git worktree; the campaign driver of inc-3 owns branching, and a worktree per cell would fragment the single monotone branch the campaign needs.

## Out of scope for this increment

The `evaluator-closure-loop` driver skill (inc-3), any change to `scripts/`, to `src/`, to `docs/agents/e2e-testcase-author.md`, to ADR 0033, and running the campaign itself. Do not author a scenario as a demonstration.

# inc-3 — the campaign driver skill `evaluator-closure-loop`

## What gets built

Exactly one new file: `.claude/skills/evaluator-closure-loop/SKILL.md`. Nothing else changes. No production code, no test, no ADR, no doc edit — `docs/project-map.md` and `docs/adr/README.md` mention skills nowhere, so neither needs an entry, and the explorer skill (inc-2) already declares that the driver owns the branch and may add its own top-level keys to `docs/testing/campaign-state.json`, so it needs no edit either.

The file is written in English (the shared brief binds every landed file to English; the explorer's body is English too — only its `description` opens with a German sentence, which we do not imitate). It is prose that a session executes: state each rule once, in the imperative.

## Frontmatter

Three keys, exactly the shape the explorer and the uroboros skills use:

```yaml
---
name: evaluator-closure-loop
description: <one sentence on what the campaign does> Use this skill when the user asks to run, continue or resume the unattended evaluator coverage-closure campaign, or when a scheduled reminder asks to continue it.
user-invocable: true
---
```

The trigger sentence must cover the self-scheduled wake-up, because the re-armed `send_later` message is what re-invokes the skill in the next session. `name` must be exactly `evaluator-closure-loop` (criterion 1) and the directory name must match it.

## The fixed constants the skill declares (one section, near the top)

- `CELL_CAP = 6` — cells per run, the fixed per-run cap (criterion 5).
- `CELLS_PER_PASS = 3` — cells per phase-A pass; a run therefore has two phase-A passes with one phase-B round between them.
- `MAX_GAP_ROUNDS = 2` — implementation rounds per pinned gap before it is parked (criterion 5).
- `RE_ARM_DELAY = 60 minutes` (criterion 4).
- `CAMPAIGN_BRANCH = claude/evaluator-coverage-campaign` — the one branch the campaign runs on.

These are values in the text, not knobs: the skill states them and the run does not negotiate them.

## Run shape (the section order of the file)

1. **What this skill does** — the driver of the unattended coverage-closure campaign: it alternates phase A (search: the `evaluator-constraint-explorer` skill pins one uncovered cell per invocation) with phase B (implement: `uroboros:agile-loop` on a campaign issue built from the open pinned gaps), keeps every fact on disk, and re-arms itself until the campaign is closed. It never authors a scenario and never edits evaluator production code itself; phase A delegates the first, phase B the second.
2. **State on disk** — the four files and who owns what:
   - `docs/testing/worklist.json` — generated by the inventory; the uncovered cells, sorted heaviest first; `totals.cells / totals.covered / totals.uncovered` are the numbers the run report quotes.
   - `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` — the manual covered/waived record; the explorer writes it, the driver only reads it.
   - `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` — `pinnedGaps` and `parkedQuestions` belong to the explorer; the driver reads them and never writes them. Everything the driver records lives under the single new top-level key `driver`.
   - the campaign issue directory under `docs/issues/` — `issue.md` (rewritten per phase-B round) plus the `backlog.json` `uroboros:agile-loop` keeps there.
   A fresh session resumes from these four alone: the skill states that no fact of the campaign is ever held only in the conversation.
3. **Step 0 — prepare the run.**
4. **Step 1 — fold in answered questions.**
5. **Step 2 — the termination check.**
6. **Step 3 — phase A pass.**
7. **Step 4 — phase B round.**
8. **Step 5 — phase A again.**
9. **Step 6 — close the run: report, then re-arm or stand down.**
10. **Never** — the closed list of prohibitions.

## The `driver` key of `campaign-state.json`

One top-level key, `driver`, holding everything the driver owns. Criterion 6 asks that the driver's state go into its own top-level keys and leave `pinnedGaps` and `parkedQuestions` to the explorer; a single owned object satisfies that separation and keeps the ownership boundary visible in one place. The skill spells the shape out so a fresh session can write it:

```json
"driver": {
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "branch": "claude/evaluator-coverage-campaign",
  "campaignIssue": "docs/issues/0147-evaluator-coverage-gaps",
  "runs": 0,
  "lastRunAt": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ",
  "lastRunOutcome": "rearmed | terminated | stopped-operational-failure | stood-down",
  "reArmedFor": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ | null",
  "consecutiveOperationalFailures": 0,
  "gaps": {
    "docs/testing/<slug>": {
      "cellKey": "<pipe-delimited cell key>",
      "attempts": 0,
      "status": "open | closed | parked",
      "lastRoundAt": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "question": null,
      "questionStatus": "open | answered",
      "answer": null
    }
  }
}
```

`gaps` is keyed by the pinned gap's `scenario` path, because that path is unique per gap while a cell key need not be. An entry appears the first time phase B works that gap. The skill states: create the `driver` key with these fields and `runs: 0` when `campaign-state.json` does not carry it yet, and never touch the two explorer arrays while doing it.

**The open task list** = every `pinnedGaps` entry with `status: "open"` whose `scenario` is not recorded in `driver.gaps` as `closed` or `parked`. That definition is what lets the driver close and park gaps without ever writing the explorer's array, and the skill states it once, in step 4, and refers back to it.

## Step 0 — prepare the run

- Refuse to start on a dirty checkout: run `git status --porcelain`; if it prints anything, stop and report, because the campaign commits per cell and per round and would otherwise sweep up someone else's work.
- Branch: read `driver.branch`. If `campaign-state.json` carries no `driver` key, this is the first run — create `claude/evaluator-coverage-campaign` off the current branch, record it, and commit the seeded `driver` key. Otherwise check out the recorded branch (`git checkout <branch>`, fetching it from the remote when the checkout does not have it). Never create a git worktree — the explorer's precondition says the driver owns the branch, and the campaign has exactly one.
- Read `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` only if this run will invoke the explorer — the explorer's own precondition asks for it and the driver's session is the same session, so state that it is read once per session before the first cell.
- Increment `driver.runs`, set `driver.lastRunAt`, commit.

## Step 1 — fold in answered questions (criterion 7)

Before any cell is taken:

- Scan `parkedQuestions` for entries with `status: "answered"`. An entry whose `answer` is null or empty is not answered: report it in the run report as still open and skip it. For a genuinely answered entry, hand its cell to the explorer first in step 3, and pass the recorded answer into the invocation so the explorer can quote it into its delegation prompt. The driver does not rewrite the entry — the explorer owns that array and its own skill already picks up an answered cell like any other worklist entry.
- Scan `driver.gaps` for entries with `status: "parked"` and `questionStatus: "answered"` with a non-empty `answer`. Reset such an entry to `attempts: 0`, `status: "open"`, so the gap re-enters the phase-B task list, and quote the answer into that gap's task text in the campaign issue.
- Commit the state change before going on.

## Step 2 — the termination check (criterion 3)

Run, in this order:

1. `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` from the repository root. Exit codes, as the script's header defines them: `0` every occurring cell covered or waived; `1` the worklist is not empty — the loop's normal state, not a failure; `2` an operational failure (missing corpus directory, `parsererror`, unreadable JSON record). A tool wrapper that flags exit 1 as an error must not be read as a failure.
   - **Exit 2 is a stop, never a termination.** End the run immediately without running any phase, increment `driver.consecutiveOperationalFailures`, set `lastRunOutcome: "stopped-operational-failure"`, report the `FAILURE` lines verbatim to the human, and re-arm as any unfinished run does — the campaign is not closed, and a human may have repaired the corpus by the next run. One bounded exception, stated as such: after three consecutive runs that stopped on an operational failure, set `lastRunOutcome: "stood-down"`, do not re-arm, and report that the campaign is standing down until a human restarts it, because an unattended loop that cannot progress must not re-arm forever. Reset the counter to 0 on any run that gets past this step.
2. `npx vitest run src/evaluator` — the evaluator suite including the manifest-driven E2E runner.
3. Read `parkedQuestions` and `driver.gaps`.

**Terminated** when all three hold at once: the inventory exited 0, the evaluator suite passed with no failing case, and no `parkedQuestions` entry and no `driver.gaps` entry is open (`status: "open"` on a parked question, or a `driver.gaps` entry with `status: "parked"`). Then: set `lastRunOutcome: "terminated"`, `reArmedFor: null`, commit and push, report the closure, and **do not call `send_later`**. That is the only condition that stops the re-arming.

Otherwise continue to phase A. The suite being red here is expected mid-campaign: every pinned gap is a committed red scenario, and `CLAUDE.md`'s "all unit tests must pass" is suspended for exactly those, as the explorer skill already records.

## Step 3 — phase A pass (criterion 2)

Up to `CELLS_PER_PASS` cells, and never past the run's remaining `CELL_CAP` budget:

- Invoke the `evaluator-constraint-explorer` skill, once per cell. It completes exactly one cell per invocation and commits that cell's work itself (scenario directory, `covered-cells.json`, regenerated `worklist.json`, Testkatalog entry, and for a red scenario its `pinnedGaps` entry). The driver adds nothing to those commits.
- Prefer the cell of an answered parked question from step 1; otherwise let the explorer take the next worklist cell by its own rule.
- Stop the pass early when the explorer reports that the worklist holds no takeable cell, or when the inventory exits 0.
- Count every invocation against the run budget, whether the cell came out green, red or parked.
- Never write a scenario, a manifest or a coverage record in the driver's own turn: authorship belongs to the `e2e-testcase-author` subagent, which only the explorer delegates to (ADR 0033).

## Step 4 — phase B round (criterion 2)

Skip the round when the open task list is empty; say so in the report.

**The campaign issue.** One issue directory for the whole campaign, recorded in `driver.campaignIssue`. Create it on the first phase-B round as `docs/issues/<NNNN>-evaluator-coverage-gaps/issue.md`, where `NNNN` is the next free four-digit number above the highest numbered entry in `docs/issues/` (0146 is the highest today, so 0147 unless it is taken). A directory, not the single-file form the repo's `CLAUDE.md` describes, because `uroboros:agile-loop` is handed an issue *directory* and keeps its `backlog.json` beside `issue.md`.

Rewrite `issue.md` before every round from the current open task list, to this shape:

```markdown
---
status: active
branch: claude/evaluator-coverage-campaign
pr:
---

# Evaluator gaps pinned by the coverage campaign

## Goal

Make every scenario listed below green by changing `src/evaluator/` production code. Each entry is a committed black-box E2E scenario whose expectations were derived from the catalog data alone; the scenario is the specification and the engine is what is wrong.

## Context

- The scenarios were authored by the `e2e-testcase-author` subagent under ADR 0033 and are pinned in `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` under `pinnedGaps`.
- `npx vitest run src/evaluator` runs the manifest-driven runner `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` over them.

## Acceptance criteria

- <one bullet per open gap: the scenario path, the failing case labels, and the gap's `note` — what the catalog data demands — plus, where the gap was parked and answered, the recorded answer quoted.>

## Out of scope

- Changing, weakening or deleting any scenario under `docs/testing/` — its `.ros` files, its `scenario.json` and its `README.md` are the specification.
- Authoring new E2E scenarios; the coverage campaign's phase A does that.
- Any change outside `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests.

## Decisions

- The check command for this issue is `npx vitest run src/evaluator`.
- No version bump inside the campaign; the human decides that when the campaign branch merges.
```

**Running the round.** With the checkout on the campaign branch, run the `uroboros:agile-loop` workflow and hand it the issue directory as `args.issueDir`. The workflow publishes whatever branch the checkout is on and merges each accepted increment back into it, so the fixes land on the campaign branch and phase A continues on top of them; it also opens the pull request itself, so the driver never opens one.

**Resuming versus starting a round.** If `<campaignIssue>/backlog.json` exists and its run is unfinished, start the same workflow on the same directory again — it resumes and skips every recorded step; never start a fresh issue directory to retry. Only when the previous round finished and new gaps are open, rename `backlog.json` to `backlog.round-<n>.json` before rewriting `issue.md`, so the new round starts from a clean run state while the record of the old one survives. Track `n` as `driver.runs` at the time of the round.

**Judging the round.** After the workflow returns, run `npx vitest run src/evaluator` and decide per gap on that run's output:

- Every case of the gap's scenario green → `driver.gaps[<scenario>].status = "closed"`.
- Still red → `attempts += 1`, `lastRoundAt` today. When `attempts` reaches `MAX_GAP_ROUNDS` (2), set `status: "parked"`, `questionStatus: "open"` and write a `question` a human can answer without opening a file — what the scenario demands, what two implementation rounds failed at, and what decision would unblock it. A parked gap leaves the task list and is never handed to another round until its question is answered (criterion 5 and 7).
- Commit the `driver` state and push the campaign branch.

## Step 5 — phase A again (criterion 2)

Run step 3 once more with the run's remaining budget, because a landed fix can make new cells reachable and because the worklist is regenerated by every inventory run. Run it even when phase B was skipped — then it is simply the search continuing.

## Step 6 — close the run

**Report to the human** (criterion 7), as the last message of the run, in this shape:

```
## Evaluator closure loop — run <driver.runs>

Coverage: <totals.covered>/<totals.cells> cells covered, <totals.uncovered> uncovered (docs/testing/worklist.json)
Phase A: <cells this run, each with its key and green/red/parked outcome>
Phase B: <campaign issue path> — closed <n>, still red <n>, parked <n>
Evaluator suite: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` — <passed>/<failed>

Parked questions waiting on you (<n>):
1. <cellKey or scenario> — <question>
   Answer it in <docs/testing/campaign-state.json>: write the answer into that entry's `answer` and set `status: "answered"` (a parked gap: `questionStatus: "answered"`).

Next run: re-armed for <local time> | none — the campaign is closed
```

List both sources of parked questions: the explorer's `parkedQuestions` entries with `status: "open"`, and `driver.gaps` entries with `status: "parked"`. Say "none" explicitly when there are none — the human must not have to guess whether the section was omitted or empty.

**Re-arm** (criterion 4). At the end of every unfinished run — including a run stopped by inventory exit 2 — call the `send_later` tool with a delay of about one hour and a message that re-invokes this skill, for example: `Continue the evaluator coverage-closure campaign: run the evaluator-closure-loop skill.` Record the scheduled time in `driver.reArmedFor` and `lastRunOutcome: "rearmed"`. Re-arm exactly once per run. If the tool is unavailable in the session, say so in the report and ask the human to re-invoke the skill in an hour — never substitute a sleep, a background process or a cron entry. Do not re-arm when the run terminated (step 2) or when the driver stood down after three consecutive operational failures.

**Commit and push.** The driver's own commits carry only `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` and the campaign issue files, with messages in the form `chore(campaign): <what changed>`. Push the campaign branch at the end of every run, so a session that dies loses nothing.

## Step 7 — the `Never` list

- Never write `pinnedGaps` or `parkedQuestions` — they belong to the explorer.
- Never author, edit, weaken or delete a scenario under `docs/testing/`, and never change a scenario's expectations to make the engine pass.
- Never change production code under `src/evaluator/` in the driver's own turn; phase B does that through `uroboros:agile-loop`.
- Never exceed `CELL_CAP` cells in one run or `MAX_GAP_ROUNDS` rounds on one gap.
- Never create a git worktree, never run the campaign on the repository's default branch, and never open a pull request yourself.
- Never keep a campaign fact only in the conversation: if a fresh session could not read it from the four state files, it does not exist.
- Never re-arm after termination.
